headline: Approved $500.00 donation for Fire Marshal's office cameras and $1,000.00 transfer of donated funds for gas meters.
summary: The meeting approved the August 27, 2026 minutes and the August monthly reports. It approved a $500.00 donation to buy cameras for the Fire Marshal's office and a $1,000.00 transfer of donated funds to buy gas meters.
decisions: Approved the August 27, 2026 meeting minutes with a correction, unanimously.
Approved the August monthly reports and placed them on file, unanimously.
Approved a $500.00 general donation to purchase cameras for the Fire Marshal's office, unanimously.
Approved a $1,000.00 transfer of donated funds to purchase gas meters, unanimously.

plain_text:
Board of Fire Commissioners’ Regular Meeting       
September 24, 2026 
 
A Regular Meeting of the Board of Fire Commissioners was held on Thursday, September 24, 
2026, at 6:00 p.m., at Bristol Fire Station 4, 17 Vincent P. Kelly Road, Bristol, CT 
 
 
Present: Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu, Commissioners Dana Jandreau, Hal Kilby, Anthony 
Benvenuto, Sandra Bogdanski, and Dannette Rodriguez, Council Member Peter Kelley, and Fire 
Chief Richard Hart 
 
1. CALL TO ORDER 
a. Mayor Zoppo-Sassu called the meeting to order at 6:00 pm. She led introductions and 
welcomed the Fall Citizens Academy attendees to the Fire Board meeting.   
  
2. EMPLOYEE RECOGNITION 
a. None. 
 
3. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION 
a. None.  
 
4. COMMUNICATIONS 
a. None.  
 
5. APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES 
a. On motion of Commissioner Kilby, seconded by Commissioner Benvenuto, it was 
unanimously voted: To approve the August 27, 2026 regular meeting minutes with the 
correction of completing the last sentence in item 6 a.   
 
6. APPROVAL OF THE MONTHLY REPORTS 
a. On motion of Commissioner Jandreau, seconded by Commissioner Benevenuto, it was 
unanimously voted: To approve the August monthly reports and place them on file.  
• Mutual Aid calls were discussed by the board. Chief Hart shared that there was 
1 Mutual Aid call, but the call was canceled it while members were en route.  
• Commissioner Bogdanski questioned the report of mold at Station 2. Chief Hart 
advised that Dave Oakes is investigating.  
• Mayor Zoppo-Sassu asked about the new Northeast Middle School survey that 
was completed by Engine 5. Chief Hart advised that the company that did the 
survey shares this information with the department by entering all information 
into First Due. Chief Hart provided an overview of how the department would 
respond to a fire alarm at Northeast Middle School.  
• Chief Hart advised that the two Ford Rangers for the replacement of two
vehicles in the Fire Marshal’s Office will be delivered in December.   
• Chief Hart shared that the UTV is in full service and department training has 
been completed.  
 
7. COMMITTEE REPORTS 
a. Fire Station 3 Building Committee 
• Chief Hart shared that the committee has not closed out the project. The 
committee is still addressing some items with the contractor.  
b. Personnel Committee 
• Commissioner Jandreau advised that recruits Firefighters Drouin and Greco are 
doing well in the Fire Academy and will complete their training in December.    
8. OLD BUSINESS 
a. None.  
 
9. NEW BUSINESS 
a. A Board of Finance Request to appropriate a donation was presented. On motion of 
Commissioner Jandreau and seconded by Commissioner Benvenuto, the Board 
unanimously approved the Board of Finance Request to appropriate $500.00 for a 
general donation to the Fire Department to purchase cameras for the Fire Marshal’s 
office.  
• Commissioner Jandreau made a motion to bring a new item up under new 
business. Commissioner Bogdanski seconded this motion. The motion passed 
unanimously. 
• A Board of Finance Request to transfer a donation was presented. 
Commissioner Jandreau moved to transfer $1,000.00 in donated funds to 
purchase gas meters, and Commissioner Benvenuto seconded. The Board 
unanimously approved the request.  
b. The Bristol Boys and Girls Club will be collaborating with the Bristol Fire Department in 
October for Fire Prevention Month. They will work with 4th- and 5th-grade students in 
their after-school programs to complete posters for the CT Fair Plan Annual Poster 
Contest.  
 
10. ADJOURN 
a. On motion of Commissioner Bentivengo and seconded by Commissioner Bogdanski, it was 
unanimously voted to adjourn the meeting at 6:30 pm. 
 
 
 
 
 
Recording Secretary: Sara Bianchi
